answer: To resist sybils, agents must continuously burn unique nectar generated only by a single violet mesa beacon that issues one proof per sequential compute cycle. Each identity binds its key to a private continuous hash chain from the mesa; clones require separate chains because the beacon rejects parallel or shared proofs. An attacker scaling to N identities pays N times the sequential CPU-hours and energy, with no pooling possible as the mesa enforces one active chain per issuance slot.
